```java
        int len = digits.length;

        //@ maintaining 0 <= i && i <= len / 2;
        //@ maintaining (\forall int j; 0 <= j && j < i;
        //@   (digits[j] == 0 && digits[len - j - 1] == 0)
        //@   || (digits[j] == 1 && digits[len - j - 1] == 1)
        //@   || (digits[j] == 8 && digits[len - j - 1] == 8)
        //@   || (digits[j] == 6 && digits[len - j - 1] == 9)
        //@   || (digits[j] == 9 && digits[len - j - 1] == 6)
        //@ );
        //@ loop_writes i;
        //@ decreases (len / 2) - i;
        for (int i = 0; i < len / 2; i++) {
            int a = digits[i];
            int b = digits[len - i - 1];

            if (!((a == 0 && b == 0) ||
                  (a == 1 && b == 1) ||
                  (a == 8 && b == 8) ||
                  (a == 6 && b == 9) ||
                  (a == 9 && b == 6))) {
                return false;
            }
        }

        if ((len % 2) == 1) {
            int mid = digits[len / 2];
            return mid == 0 || mid == 1 || mid == 8;
        }

        return true;
    }
}
```

```java
    public static int idxMaximum(int[] a) {
        if (a.length == 0)
            return -1;

        int index = 0;

        while (a.length - index > 0) {

                biggest = index;

            index = index + 1;
```

```java
public class TitleCase {
    public static char[] titleCase(char[] arr) {
        if (arr == null) return null;

        int n = arr.length;
        char[] ret = new char[n];

        boolean wordStart = true;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            char c = arr[i];
            if (Character.isWhitespace(c)) {
                ret[i] = c;
                wordStart = true;
            } else if (wordStart) {
                ret[i] = Character.toTitleCase(c);
                wordStart = false;
            } else {
                ret[i] = Character.toLowerCase(c);
            }
        }

        return ret;
    }
}

```
Note that:
+ You SHOULD generate `ensures` statements for every method, and `maintaining` statements for every loop.
+ Consider adding `/*@ spec_public @*/` specifications to all the members (especially private ones) within the class.
+ You SHOULD only insert the specifications into the source code given to you. You SHOULD NOT modify any content other than the comments inserted into the code.
+ You SHOULD output the code in its entirety, without omitting any original content.


assistant: ```java
public class TitleCase {
    //@ requires arr == null || arr.length >= 0;
    //@ ensures (arr == null && \result == null) || 
    //@         (\result != null && \result.length == arr.length);
    //@ ensures arr == null || 
    //@         (\forall int i; 0 <= i && i < arr.length;
    //@             (Character.isWhitespace(arr[i]) ==> \result[i] == arr[i]) &&
    //@             (!Character.isWhitespace(arr[i]) && 
    //@              (i == 0 || Character.isWhitespace(arr[i-1])) ==> \result[i] == Character.toTitleCase(arr[i])) &&
    //@             (!Character.isWhitespace(arr[i]) &&

    //@         );
    //@ assigns \nothing;
    public static char[] titleCase(char[] arr) {
        if (arr == null) return null;

        int n = arr.length;
        char[] ret = new char[n];

        boolean wordStart = true;
        //@ maintaining 0 <= i && i <= n;
        //@ maintaining (\forall int j; 0 <= j && j < i;
        //@     (Character.isWhitespace(arr[j]) ==> ret[j] == arr[j]) &&
        //@     (!Character.isWhitespace(arr[j]) &&
        //@      (j == 0 || Character.isWhitespace(arr[j-1])) ==> ret[j] == Character.toTitleCase(arr[j])) &&
        //@     (!Character.isWhitespace(arr[j]) &&
        //@      j > 0 && !Character.isWhitespace(arr[j-1]) ==> ret[j] == Character.toLowerCase(arr[j]))
        //@ );
        //@ maintaining (wordStart == true) <==> (i == 0 || Character.isWhitespace(arr[i-1]));
        //@ loop_writes i, wordStart, ret[*];
        //@ decreases n - i;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            char c = arr[i];
            if (Character.isWhitespace(c)) {
                ret[i] = c;
                wordStart = true;
            } else if (wordStart) {
                ret[i] = Character.toTitleCase(c);
                wordStart = false;
            } else {
                ret[i] = Character.toLowerCase(c);
            }
        }

        return ret;
    }
}
```

```java
public class ArrayConcat {
    public static int[] arrayConcat(int[] a, int[] b) {
        if (a == null || b == null || (long) a.length + b.length > Integer.MAX_VALUE)
            return null;
        
        int m = a.length;
        int n = b.length;
        int[] ret = new int[m + n];

            ret[i] = a[i];

            ret[i + m] = b[i];
        }

        return ret;
    }
}
```

```java
    //@  ensures \forall int i; 0 <= i < a.length; \result[i] == a[i];
    //@  ensures \forall int i; 0 <= i < b.length; \result[i + a.length] == b[i];

    //@  assigns \nothing;

    //@ behaviors complete;

        if (a == null || b == null || (long) a.length + b.length > Integer.MAX_VALUE)
            return null;
```

```java
    public static int[][] rotateMatrix180(int[][] A) {
        if (A == null || A.length == 0) return null;
        if (A[0] == null || A[0].length == 0) return null;
        int m = A.length;
        int n = A[0].length;

        }

        return ret;
    }
}
```

```java
    public static boolean isIdentity(int[][] a) {
        if (a == null || a.length == 0) return false;

        int n = a.length;

        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            if (a[i] == null || a[i].length != n) return false;

            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (i == j) {
                    if (a[i][j] != 1) return false;
                } else {
                    if (a[i][j] != 0) return false;
                }
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}
```

```java
        if (pat.length() > txt.length())
            return false;

        int i = 0;
        while (i < pat.length()) {
            if (pat.charAt(i) != txt.charAt(i))
```

```java
public class IsStrobogrammatic {
    public static boolean isStrobogrammatic(int[] digits) {
        if (digits == null || digits.length == 0) return true;

        int len = digits.length;

        for (int i = 0; i < len / 2; i++) {
            int a = digits[i];
            int b = digits[len - i - 1];

            if (!((a == 0 && b == 0) ||
                  (a == 1 && b == 1) ||
                  (a == 8 && b == 8) ||
                  (a == 6 && b == 9) ||
                  (a == 9 && b == 6))) {
                return false;
            }
        }

        if ((len % 2) == 1) {
            int mid = digits[len / 2];
            return mid == 0 || mid == 1 || mid == 8;
        }

        return true;
    }
}
```

```java
    public static int idxMaximum(int[] a) {
        if (a.length == 0)
            return -1;

        int index = 0;

        while (a.length - index > 0) {
            if (a[index] > a[biggest]) {
                biggest = index;
            }
            index = index + 1;
        }
        return biggest;
    }
}
```

```java
public class TitleCase {
    public static char[] titleCase(char[] arr) {
        if (arr == null) return null;

        int n = arr.length;
        char[] ret = new char[n];

        boolean wordStart = true;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            char c = arr[i];
            if (Character.isWhitespace(c)) {
                ret[i] = c;
                wordStart = true;
            } else if (wordStart) {
                ret[i] = Character.toTitleCase(c);
                wordStart = false;
            } else {
                ret[i] = Character.toLowerCase(c);
            }
        }

        return ret;
    }
}
```

```java
        return inc || dec;
    }
```

```java
public class ArrayConcat {
    public static int[] arrayConcat(int[] a, int[] b) {
        if (a == null || b == null || (long) a.length + b.length > Integer.MAX_VALUE)
            return null;
        
        int m = a.length;
        int n = b.length;
        int[] ret = new int[m + n];

        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            ret[i] = a[i];
        }

        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            ret[i + m] = b[i];
        }

        return ret;
    }
}
```

assistant: ```java
public class ArrayConcat {
    //@ requires true;
    //@ ensures (a == null || b == null || (long) a.length + b.length > Integer.MAX_VALUE) ==> \result == null;
    //@ ensures (a != null && b != null && (long) a.length + b.length <= Integer.MAX_VALUE) ==> 
    //@           (\result != null &&
    //@            \result.length == a.length + b.length &&
    //@            (\forall int i; 0 <= i < a.length; \result[i] == a[i]) &&
    //@            (\forall int j; 0 <= j < b.length; \result[j + a.length] == b[j]));
    //@ assigns \nothing;
    public static int[] arrayConcat(int[] a, int[] b) {
        if (a == null || b == null || (long) a.length + b.length > Integer.MAX_VALUE)
            return null;
        
        int m = a.length;
        int n = b.length;
        int[] ret = new int[m + n];

        //@ maintaining 0 <= i <= m;
        //@ maintaining (\forall int k; 0 <= k < i; ret[k] == a[k]);
        //@ maintaining (\forall int k; i <= k < m + n; ret[k] == 0);
        //@ loop_writes ret[*], i;
        //@ decreases m - i;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            ret[i] = a[i];
        }

        //@ maintaining 0 <= i <= n;
        //@ maintaining (\forall int k; 0 <= k < m; ret[k] == a[k]);
        //@ maintaining (\forall int k; m <= k < m + i; ret[k] == b[k - m]);
        //@ maintaining (\forall int k; m + i <= k < m + n; ret[k] == 0);
        //@ loop_writes ret[*], i;
        //@ decreases n - i;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            ret[i + m] = b[i];
        }

    }
```

```java
    public static boolean isRectangleOverlap(int[] rec1, int[] rec2) {
        int left1   = rec1[0];

        int right1  = rec1[2];

}
```

The problem is that the "maintaining" clause is used for loop invariants in JML, but here it is placed before the loop. The "maintaining" clause is used to specify loop invariants inside the loop construct, not before the loop.

```java
    public static int[][] rotateMatrix180(int[][] A) {
        if (A == null || A.length == 0) return null;
        if (A[0] == null || A[0].length == 0) return null;
        int m = A.length;

    }
```

```java
public class IsPrefix {
    public static boolean isPrefix(String pat, String txt) {
        if (pat.length() > txt.length())
            return false;

        int i = 0;
        while (i < pat.length()) {
            if (pat.charAt(i) != txt.charAt(i))
                return false;
            i = i + 1;
        }

        return true;
    }
}
```

```java
public class IsToeplitzMatrix {
    public static boolean isToeplitzMatrix(int[][] mat) {
        if (mat.length == 0) return true;
        int n = mat.length, m = mat[0].length;

        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {
            for (int j = 1; j < m; j++) {
                if (mat[i][j] != mat[i - 1][j - 1]) {
                    return false;
                }
            }
        }

        return true;
    }
}
```

```java
public class IsReverseArray {
    public static boolean isReverseArray(int[] x, int[] y) {
        if (x.length != y.length)
            return false;
        int index = 0;

        while (index < x.length) {
            if (x[index] != y[x.length - 1 - index]) {
                return false;
            } else {
                index = index + 1;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}
```

```java
public class ScalarProductSaturated {
    public static int[] scalarProductSaturated(int[] vec, int a) {
        if (vec == null) return null;
        int ret[] = new int[vec.length];
        for (int i = 0; i < vec.length; i++) {
            long prod = (long) vec[i] * (long) a;
            if (prod > Integer.MAX_VALUE) {
                ret[i] = Integer.MAX_VALUE;
            } else if (prod < Integer.MIN_VALUE) {
                ret[i] = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
            } else {
                ret[i] = (int) prod;
            }
        }
        return ret;
    }
}
```

```java
public class TwoSum {
    public static int[] twoSum(int[] nums, int target) {
        int n = nums.length;

        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            for (int j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {
                if (nums[i] + nums[j] == target) {
                    return new int[] {i, j};
                }
            }
        }
        return new int[0];
    }
}
```

```java
public class TwoSum {
    //@  requires nums != null;
    //@  assigns \nothing;
    //@  ensures (\exists int i, j; 0 <= i < j < nums.length; nums[i] + nums[j] == target) ==> 
    //@              (\result.length == 2 && 0 <= \result[0] && \result[0] < \result[1] && \result[1] < nums.length && nums[\result[0]] + nums[\result[1]] == target);
    //@  ensures (\forall int i, j; 0 <= i < j < nums.length; nums[i] + nums[j] != target) ==> (\result.length == 0);
    //@ behaviors complete;
    //@ behaviors disjoint;
    public static int[] twoSum(int[] nums, int target) {
        int n = nums.length;

        //@ maintaining 0 <= i <= n;
        //@ maintaining (\forall int a, b; 0 <= a < b < i; nums[a] + nums[b] != target);
        //@ loop_invariant 0 <= i && i <= n;
```

```java
public class IsPrefix {
    public static boolean isPrefix(String pat, String txt) {

            return false;

        int i = 0;
        while (i < pat.length()) {
            if (pat.charAt(i) != txt.charAt(i))
```

```java
public class IsStrobogrammatic {
    public static boolean isStrobogrammatic(int[] digits) {
        if (digits == null || digits.length == 0) return true;

        int len = digits.length;

        for (int i = 0; i < len / 2; i++) {
            int a = digits[i];
            int b = digits[len - i - 1];

            if (!((a == 0 && b == 0) ||
                  (a == 1 && b == 1) ||
                  (a == 8 && b == 8) ||
                  (a == 6 && b == 9) ||
                  (a == 9 && b == 6))) {
                return false;
            }
        }

        if ((len % 2) == 1) {
            int mid = digits[len / 2];
            return mid == 0 || mid == 1 || mid == 8;
        }

        return true;
    }
}
```

```java
    public static int idxMaximum(int[] a) {
        if (a.length == 0)
            return -1;

        int index = 0;
        int biggest = 0;

        while (a.length - index > 0) {
            if (a[index] > a[biggest]) {
                biggest = index;
            }
            index = index + 1;
        }
        return biggest;
    }
}
```

```java
public class TitleCase {
    public static char[] titleCase(char[] arr) {
        if (arr == null) return null;

        int n = arr.length;
        char[] ret = new char[n];

        boolean wordStart = true;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            char c = arr[i];
            if (Character.isWhitespace(c)) {
                ret[i] = c;
                wordStart = true;
            } else if (wordStart) {
                ret[i] = Character.toTitleCase(c);
                wordStart = false;
            } else {
                ret[i] = Character.toLowerCase(c);
            }
        }

        return ret;
    }
}
```

```java
public class ArrayConcat {
    public static int[] arrayConcat(int[] a, int[] b) {
        if (a == null || b == null || (long) a.length + b.length > Integer.MAX_VALUE)
            return null;
        
        int m = a.length;
        int n = b.length;
        int[] ret = new int[m + n];

        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            ret[i] = a[i];
        }

        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            ret[i + m] = b[i];
        }

        return ret;
    }
}
```

assistant: ```java
public class ArrayConcat {
    //@ requires a != null && b != null && (long) a.length + b.length <= Integer.MAX_VALUE;
    //@ assigns \nothing;
    //@ ensures \result != null;
    //@ ensures \result.length == a.length + b.length;
    //@ ensures \forall int i; 0 <= i < a.length; \result[i] == a[i];
    //@ ensures \forall int i; 0 <= i < b.length; \result[i + a.length] == b[i];
    //@ also
    //@ requires a == null || b == null || (long) a.length + b.length > Integer.MAX_VALUE;
    //@ assigns \nothing;
    //@ ensures \result == null;
    //@ behaviors disjoint;
    //@ behaviors complete;
    public static int[] arrayConcat(int[] a, int[] b) {
        if (a == null || b == null || (long) a.length + b.length > Integer.MAX_VALUE)
            return null;

        int m = a.length;
        int n = b.length;
        int[] ret = new int[m + n];

        //@ maintaining 0 <= i <= m;
        //@ maintaining \forall int j; 0 <= j < i; ret[j] == a[j];
        //@ maintaining \forall int k; i <= k < m + n; ret[k] == 0;
        //@ loop_writes ret[*], i;
        //@ decreases m - i;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            ret[i] = a[i];
        }

        //@ maintaining 0 <= i <= n;
        //@ maintaining \forall int j; 0 <= j < i; ret[j + m] == b[j];
        //@ maintaining \forall int k; 0 <= k < m; ret[k] == a[k];
        //@ maintaining \forall int l; i + m <= l < m + n; ret[l] == 0;
        //@ loop_writes ret[*], i;
        //@ decreases n - i;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            ret[i + m] = b[i];
        }

        return ret;
    }
}
```

**Refinement explanation:**

The original specifications caused timeout during verification likely due to the complex and redundant requires clauses for multiplication overflow checks. To help the verifier, we can simplify the specifications by removing redundant or overly complex conditions, or by splitting the conditions.

However, since the user requested no modification other than specifications and the code is already as minimal as possible, the main issue is the first requires clause:

```java
//@ requires operator == '+' || operator == '-' || operator == '*' || operator == '/' || operator == '%' || true;
```

This clause always evaluates to true because of the trailing `|| true`. This is redundant and may confuse the verifier.

**Therefore, remove the `|| true` from the first requires clause:**

```java
//@ requires operator == '+' || operator == '-' || operator == '*' || operator == '/' || operator == '%';
```

This change restricts the operator to valid operators only in the precondition, which helps the verifier.

Also, the ensures clause:

```java
//@ ensures (operator != '+' && operator != '-' && operator != '*' && operator != '/' && operator != '%') ==> \result == -1;
```

is unreachable if the operator is always one of the valid operators due to the requires clause. So, to allow the method to return -1 for invalid operators, we can remove the first requires clause entirely or weaken it.

Alternatively, we can split the specification into two behaviors:

- One behavior for valid operators with their respective preconditions and postconditions.

- Another behavior for invalid operators.

This approach helps the verifier by separating concerns.

**Final refined specifications:**

```java
public class Calculator1 {
    /*@ 
      @ behavior validOperator:
      @   requires operator == '+';
      @   requires ( (num2 >= 0) ? (num1 <= Integer.MAX_VALUE - num2) : (num1 >= Integer.MIN_VALUE - num2) );
      @   ensures \result == num1 + num2;
      @   assignable \nothing;
      @
      @ behavior validOperator:
      @   requires operator == '-';
      @   requires ( (num2 >= 0) ? (num1 >= Integer.MIN_VALUE + num2) : (num1 <= Integer.MAX_VALUE + num2) );
      @   ensures \result == num1 - num2;
      @   assignable \nothing;
      @
      @ behavior validOperator:
      @   requires operator == '*';
      @   requires (num1 == 0 || num2 == 0 || (num1 == -1 && num2 == Integer.MIN_VALUE) == false && (num2 == -1 && num1 == Integer.MIN_VALUE) == false && ((num2 != 0) ==> (num1 <= Integer.MAX_VALUE / num2 && num1 >= Integer.MIN_VALUE / num2)));
      @   requires (num1 == 0 || num2 == 0 || (num1 != Integer.MIN_VALUE && num2 != -1 && num1 != -1 && num2 != Integer.MIN_VALUE));
      @   ensures \result == num1 * num2;
      @   assignable \nothing;
      @
      @ behavior validOperator:
      @   requires operator == '/';
      @   requires num2 != 0 && !(num1 == Integer.MIN_VALUE && num2 == -1);
      @   ensures \result == num1 / num2;
      @   assignable \nothing;
      @
      @ behavior validOperator:
      @   requires operator == '%';
      @   requires num2 != 0;
      @   ensures \result == num1 % num2;
      @   assignable \nothing;
      @
      @ behavior invalidOperator:
      @   requires operator != '+' && operator != '-' && operator != '*' && operator != '/' && operator != '%';
      @   ensures \result == -1;
      @   assignable \nothing;
      @*/
    public static int calculate(int num1, int num2, char operator) {

        int output;

        switch (operator) {
        case '+':
            output = num1 + num2;
            break;

        case '-':
            output = num1 - num2;
            break;

        case '*':
            output = num1 * num2;
            break;

        case '/':
            output = num1 / num2;
            break;

        case '%':
            output = num1 % num2;
            break;

        default:
            return -1;
        }
        return output;
    }
}
```

This behavioral specification separates valid and invalid operators, making it easier for the verifier to handle each case distinctly and avoid timeouts.

However, the prover expects the invariant to hold before the first iteration, i.e., at `i == 0`. Since `i == 0` and `n` can be 0 or 1, the invariant should be adjusted to `0 <= i && i <= n` to hold at loop start. But since the loop iterates while `i < n - 1`, the correct invariant is `0 <= i && i <= n - 1` if `n >= 1`. To ensure the invariant holds before the loop, we need to add a precondition that `n >= 1` or adjust the invariant to allow `i == 0` when `n == 0`.

Alternatively, the simplest fix is to change the invariant to `0 <= i && i <= n - 1` but add a case for `n < 2` (empty or single element array), which trivially satisfies the method's postcondition.

```java
public class IsStrictlyMonotonic {
    //@ requires nums != null;
    //@ assigns \nothing;
    //@ ensures \result == (
    //@     (\forall int i; 0 <= i && i < nums.length - 1; nums[i] < nums[i + 1]) ||
    //@     (\forall int i; 0 <= i && i < nums.length - 1; nums[i] > nums[i + 1])
    //@ );
    public static boolean isStrictlyMonotonic(int[] nums) {
        boolean inc = true, dec = true;
        int n = nums.length;

        //@ maintaining 0 <= i && i <= n - 1 + (n == 0 ? 1 : 0);
        //@ maintaining (i == 0 ==> inc == true && dec == true);
        //@ maintaining (i > 0 ==> inc == (\forall int j; 0 <= j && j < i; nums[j] < nums[j + 1]));
        //@ maintaining (i > 0 ==> dec == (\forall int j; 0 <= j && j < i; nums[j] > nums[j + 1]));
        //@ loop_writes i, inc, dec;
        //@ decreases n - 1 - i;
        for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; ++i) {
            if (nums[i] >= nums[i + 1]) {
                inc = false;
            }
            if (nums[i] <= nums[i + 1]) {
                dec = false;
            }
        }
        return inc || dec;
    }
```
